credit: Written for the app from Grandport's city data. Grandport is from Neokosmos, a dark fantasy world by Oak (https://quietoak.github.io/NeokosmosWiki/), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The factions follow the wiki; their quarrels are extrapolated.

factions.name: The Merchant Circle
factions.about: The founders of the Republic, who rule from the Circle Hall and the counting houses.

factions.name: The Ledger men
factions.about: Readers of Thorne's Ledger of Liberty, who think the Revolution was meant for more than the rich.

factions.name: The Admiralty
factions.about: The Republic's navy and harbour watch, loyal to Admiral Horne.

factions.name: The guilds
factions.about: Masons, carpenters, insurers and the rest, who keep the fire rules and the settling marks.

factions.name: The royalists
factions.about: Old Gran Porte families who whisper "what sank may yet rise" and wait for the exiled prince.

factions.name: The mission of Sol Eternel
factions.about: Missionaries of the Sun from the Alnhaman coast, preaching on the quays.

factions.name: The Ruestrian envoys
factions.about: Agents of the Empire across the water, buying friends with cheap red wine and cheaper loans.

factions.name: The Lower Stairs
factions.about: The poor quarter that held out through the siege on relief bread, and remembers who fed it.

questions.title: Ruestrian harbour rights
questions.question: Should Ruestrian ships be given their own berths at the Grand Quay?

sides.name: Open the berths
sides.stand: give the Empire its berths and the trade that comes with them

sides.name: Keep them out
sides.stand: keep the Empire's ships at Strangers' Wharf

beats: A Ruestrian galley was turned away from the Grand Quay.
Ruestrian red is cheaper than ever on the wharf.
An envoy dined at Grandeholm Tower.
The signal tower flew the warning colours for a Ruestrian squadron.
Dockworkers threatened to walk off if the berths are given.

questions.title: The exiled prince
questions.question: Should the Circle hunt down the royalists, or let them grumble?

sides.name: Root them out
sides.stand: root the royalists out before they try something

beats: A crowned horse was chalked on a wall in Old Gran Porte.
A royalist pamphlet turned up at the Inkwell.
The Admiralty searched a house on Kings Fall Street.
An old royalist was given a pension by the Circle.

issues.title: The price of relief bread
issues.question: Should the Circle keep paying for cheap bread in the Lower Stairs?

sides.name: End the dole
sides.stand: end it; the siege is ten years gone

beats.whispers: The relief bread hall is said to be closing.
beats.open: The Circle names the day the cheap bread ends.
beats.heated: The Lower Stairs march up the Hundred Steps with siege loaves.
beats.fizzled: The price goes up a little and nobody marches.

issues.title: Wyrmscraft's voyage
issues.question: Should the Circle fund Eadric Wyrmscraft's voyage to prove his longitude?

sides.name: Waste of coin
sides.stand: keep the money in the counting houses

beats.whispers: Wyrmscraft is asking the Circle for a ship.
beats.heated: Wyrmscraft calls the Circle cowards at the Compass Rose.
beats.fizzled: Wyrmscraft goes back to his book.

issues.title: Preaching on the quays
issues.question: Should the Sun's missionaries be let to preach on the Grand Quay?

beats.whispers: A missionary preached to the dockhands at dawn.
beats.open: The dock office asks the Circle to rule.
beats.heated: A sermon on the quay ends in a brawl.
beats.won: The missionaries may preach on the quay.
beats.lost: Preaching is kept to the chapel.
beats.fizzled: The mission sails on to another port.
